title: Mario Party 6
subtitle: The same board after sunset
summary: Mario Party 6 is Hudson Soft's GameCube party game, first released in Japan on 18 November 2004.
body: Mario Party 6 is Hudson Soft's GameCube party game, first released in Japan on 18 November 2004. Its boards change between day and night, giving the usual race for Stars a visible cycle. Brighton and Twila represent the sun and moon as the gathering moves through different conditions. Players still roll dice, use items and compete in minigames, but a place seen earlier may work differently when reached again. The board becomes something to remember across time as well as a route towards the next prize.

The light changes every three turns, altering spaces, characters and some minigame conditions. A useful route can therefore depend on when a player expects to arrive. Orbs provide effects to use or place around the board, and their importance extends to the final bonus awards. The day-and-night system gives decisions a shared clock: everyone can see the coming change, but a dice roll or another player's item may upset the timing of a carefully planned arrival.

The game introduced a GameCube microphone accessory for dedicated voice-controlled activities, adding another form of input to the party. Other minigames retain controller-based movement and reactions, making the microphone one part of a broader collection rather than the only way to take part. Hironobu Yahata and Shinya Outouge composed the score. The most distinctive change remains the board's cycle, which gives a familiar party structure a sense of passing time and lets the same themed location produce another situation when darkness falls.
story_headings: Plan for the next change of light
